notes4.Name: --alpha Gem AB
notes4.Note: X-ray flaring in the alpha Gem AB quadruple is thought to arise from the Ab and Bb members (Stelzer2003), so we chose mass estimates for these two stars that encompass the range from late-K through late-M. The WDS cites a delta mag of 1.04 mag (presumably at V band) for the AB pair. If we assume that most of the flux for A and B are emitted from Aa and Ba, then the absolute V magnitude of Ba corresponds to a spectral type of roughly A5, which corresponds to a mass of roughly 1.8 Msun. If we sum the four mass estimates for Aa, Ab, Ba, and Bb, we obtain a total mass that is within 0.1 Msun of the total dynamical mass obtained by Malkov2012.

notes4.Note: See Vrijmoet2022, who measure a median delta I of 2.7 mag. This, when combined with the composite spectral type, can be used to estimate individual types of M4 and M6, which we use for the individual mass estimates.

notes4.Name: iota Peg
notes4.Note: SB (Ren2013). STT 596B is not associated with this system (WDS).

notes4.Name: --iota Peg Aa
notes4.Note: Boden1999 derived a dynamical mass of 1.326+/-0.016 M_Sun.

notes4.Name: --iota Peg Ab
notes4.Note: Boden1999 derived a synamical mass of 0.819+/-0.009 M_Sun.

notes4.Name: WISEA J221140.53-475826.7
notes4.Note: Estimated spectral type T8 (Tinney2018).

notes4.Name: Wolf 1561 AB
notes4.Note: VGT 5C is assumed to be unassociated with this system. See Bergfors2016 for more info on this system.

notes4.Name: --Wolf 1561 B
notes4.Note: Is itself a double (Bergfors2010). Bergfors2010 estimate individual types of M4 and M8.5, which we use for our individual mass estimates.

notes4.Name: UCAC3 111-489380 AB
notes4.Note: Double (Vrijmoet2022). Vrijmoet2022 measures a median delta I of 0.0 mag. Using the G_BP-G_RP, J-Ks, and J-W2 colors, we estimate a composite spectral type of M6, which we assume is also the type of the individual components. We use these to estimate the individual masses.

notes4.Name: --HD 211415 B
notes4.Note: Gaia eDR3 has two equal-mag sources within 0.7 arcsec of this position, and neither has a parallax or proper motion.

notes4.Name: 2MASSW J2224438-015852 AB
notes4.Note: ALP 28B is not associated (WDS). Best2021 list this as a binary.

notes4.Name: 53 Aqr AB
notes4.Note: Gaia eDR3 has two equal-mag sources within 1.2 arcsec of this position (A and Ba+Bb), but neither has a proper motion or parallax. We take the G1 spectral type of the primary to estimate its mass, and we take the G5 composite type of the secondary as the type of Ba. The WDS lists a delta mag of 6.45 mag (presumably at V band) between Ba and Bb, from which we estimate a type of Bb of M3. We use this for the mass estimate of Bb. Our total mass estimate of 2.39 M_Sun is in reasonable agreement with the total dynamical mass estimate of 2.22 M_Sun in Cvetkovic2010, given that it lacks a quoted uncertainty.

notes4.Name: --53 Aqr B
notes4.Note: SB from Willmarth2016 with period of 257.3 days.

notes4.Name: CWISE J222701.50+260450.0
notes4.Note: Estimates are distance 20.0 pc and spectral type Y0 (Kirkpatrick2024).

notes4.Name: HD 239960 AB
notes4.Note: Tamazian2006 derive a total dynamical mass of 0.44+/-0.02 M_Sun. KR 60C, E, F, G, H, I; HEL 4J; FYM 118L, M, O, R, S and U are not associated with this system (WDS); this is also true of HZE 5K (WDS Notes). KR 60D is assumed not to be associated either.

notes4.Name: --HD 239960 A
notes4.Note: Gaia eDR3 has no parallax or proper motion for this component.

notes4.Name: --HD 239960 B
notes4.Note: Gaia eDR3 has no parallax or proper motion for this component. Gaia DR3 lists this as a possible LPV!

notes4.Name: CWISE J223002.32+424655.3
notes4.Note: Estimates are distance 19.8 pc and spectral type T7.5 (Kirkpatrick2024). Banyan Sigma gives this object a 97.5% probability of belonging to the Argus young moving group.

notes4.Name: LEHPM 4771 AB
notes4.Note: Double (Vrijmoet2020). See also Vrijmoet2022, who measures a median delta I of 1.1 mag. Using the composite type of M4.5, we estimate component spectral types of M4.5 and M5.5, which we use to estimate the individual masses.

notes4.Name: CWISEP J223022.60+254907.5
notes4.Note: Estimated spectral type >=Y1 (Meisner2020a).

notes4.Name: HD 214100 AB
notes4.Note: Endl2006 find a small linear trend with the radial velocities, indicative of a companion in a wide orbit. This is likely caused by the 0.6-0.7-arcsec separated B companion first observed by Jodar2013 and confirmed by Tokovinin2021, who measures a median delta I of 3.85 mag. Using the composite type, we estimate individual spectral types of M1 and M5.5, which we use for the individual mass estimates.

notes4.Name: L 119-21 AB
notes4.Note: Double (Lindegren1997). Gaia eDR3 lists *three* near equal-mag sources within 1 arcsec of one another; none has a parallax or proper motion. That having been stated, the third component mentioned in Bergfors2010 from SIMBAD is likely the GJ 9791 misprint that was a duplication in the Gliese Catalog of GJ 865 itself. The WDS quotes a delta mag of 0.13 mag (presumably at V band). We use the composite type as the type of each individual component, and use those types to estimate the individual masses.

notes4.Name: EZ Aqr ABC
notes4.Note: Triple (Delfosse1999b). This source has no parallax or proper motion solution in either Gaia DR2 or eDR3.

notes4.Name: FK Aqr & FL Aqr
notes4.Note: See Davison2014 on this quadruple.

notes4.Name: --FK Aqr
notes4.Note: SB2 with P = 4.1 day (WDS Notes). See Baroch2018. Gaia DR3 has NSS=3 -- two_body_orbit OrbitalTargetedSearch w/ period=8.0d and SB2C w/ period= 4.1d. It is assumed that these two solutions refer to the same physical pair, given the factor of (approximately) two between the two measured periods. Given that this is an SB2, we assume that both components have ~M2 spectral types and we base our individual mass estimates on that assumption.

notes4.Name: --FL Aqr
notes4.Note: SB1 with P = 1.8 day (WDS Notes). The second component in this subsystem could be a brown dwarf, according to WDS Notes. We use the composite spectral type as the estimated type of the Aa component, then we adopt a wide range to cover the estimated masses of the Ab component.

notes4.Name: WISEA J224319.56-145857.3
notes4.Note: Expected parallax is 68.3 mas (Kirkpatrick2021a) and estimated spectral type is Y0 (Meisner2020b).

notes4.Name: 2MASSW J2244316+204343
notes4.Note: Source has no entry in Gaia DR2 or eDR3.

notes4.Name: CWISE J224547.21-433341.5
notes4.Note: Estimates are distance 17.5 pc and spectral type T8 (Kirkpatrick2024).

notes4.Name: xi Peg AB
notes4.Note: HJ 301C is assumed to be unassociated with this system.

notes4.Name: EV Lac
notes4.Note: HER 5B, HER 5C, TNN 17D, and TNN 17E are assumed to be unassociated with this star.

notes4.Name: EGGR 283 AB
notes4.Note: Called a double degenerate candidate by Toonen2017. Gaia DR3 has NSS=1 -- two_body_orbit Orbital w/ period=278.0d.

notes4.Name: GT Peg
notes4.Note: LAF 70B, C, D, and E are assumed to be unassociated with this star.

notes4.Name: --DENIS-P J225210.73-173013.4 A
notes4.Note: Estimated spectral type is L4: (Dupuy2017).

notes4.Name: --DENIS-P J225210.73-173013.4 B
notes4.Note: Estimated spectral type is T3.5 (Dupuy2017).

notes4.Name: BD-15 6290
notes4.Note: 'Gaia DR3 has NSS=1 -- two_body_orbit OrbitalTargetedSearchValidated w/ period=61.4d. This is a detection of the ''b'' planet.'

notes4.Name: WISEA J225404.16-265257.5
notes4.Note: Expected parallax is 63.0 mas (Kirkpatrick2021a) and estimated spectral type is T9.5 (Meisner2020b).

notes4.Name: WISEPC J225540.74-311841.8
notes4.Note: As the discovery paper suggests, HUE 2B is probably a background galaxy.

notes4.Name: CWISEP J225628.97+400227.3
notes4.Note: Estimated spectral type >=Y1 (Meisner2020a).

notes4.Name: 51 Peg
notes4.Note: Candidate companion, RBR 21B, remains unconfirmed (WDS Notes).

notes4.Name: --alpha PsA
notes4.Note: We adopt the mass estimate from Mamajek2012.

notes4.Name: --LP 876-10
notes4.Note: It is unclear which double star candidate WSI 138 refers to.

notes4.Name: HD 217486 AB
notes4.Note: Goldin2007 find that this is a binary. There is no parallax or proper motion for this object in Gaia eDR3. We use the composite spectral type as the type of the primary, and use that as teh basis for its mass estimate. We adopt a wide range of possible lower masses for the secondary.

notes4.Name: HD 217580 AB
notes4.Note: SB. Secondary could be a brown dwarf, but see a rebuttal by Mitrofanova2021. We take the composite type to be that of the primary, and base its mass estimate on that. We adopt a wide range of possible lower masses for the secondary's estimate.

notes4.Name: CWISEP J230158.30-645858.3
notes4.Note: Expected parallax is 56.8 mas (Kirkpatrick2021a) and estimated spectral type is T8.5 (Meisner2020a).

notes4.Name: WISEA J230228.66-713441.7
notes4.Note: Estimated spectral type is T4.5 (Tinney2018).

notes4.Name: L 358-24 AB
notes4.Note: Double (Mason2018b). Object has no parallax or proper motion solution in Gaia eDR3. Gaia DR3 lists this as a possible LPV! The WDS lists a delta magnitude of only 0.1 mag, so we assume that both components have the type of the composite system. We use these types to estimate the individual masses. The G_BP-G_RP, J-Ks, and J-W2 colors suggest a composite type of M4.5.

notes4.Name: HD 217987
notes4.Note: WardDuong2015 claim that this is a double, but the secondary is not seen by Vrijmoet2022. The Jeffers2020 paper on the exoplanet system makes no mention of the secondary star.

notes4.Name: CWISE J230930.81+145630.6
notes4.Note: Distance estimate is 16.2 pc (Kirkpatrick2024).

notes4.Name: LP 822-37 AB
notes4.Note: 'Spectrophotometric distance estimate places this binary at ~20 pc (Kirkpatrick2024). The WDS lists a delta ''red'' magnitude of 0.0 mag, so we assume that both components have a type identical to that of the composite system, and we use this to estimate the individual masses.'

notes4.Name: HD 219134
notes4.Note: STT 599B is unassociated (WDS Notes) as is TNN 18E (WDS). CSN 14C, CSN 14D, TNN 18F, and TNN 18G are assumed to be unassociated with this star as well. For the mass estimate, we use the M_Ks relation.

notes4.Name: G 190-17 AB
notes4.Note: SB2 (Fouque2018). HDS 3319A is not associated with this system (Gaia DR2). It's not clear which object CRI 29A refers to. Given that this is an SB2, we tentatively assume that both components are identical and have the same type as the composite system. The individual masses are based on this assumption.

notes4.Name: G 67-53 AB
notes4.Note: 'Double (Janson2012). Listed as an SB1 in Durkan2018. ''Very rapid'' orbital motion in Janson2014b. Beuzit2004 measure a delta J of 1.17 mag. Using the composite type and this delta magnitude, we estimate component types of M3.5 and M5, which we use for our mass estimates.'

notes4.Name: --HD 220140 AB
notes4.Note: LAF 72D and E are assumed to be unassociated with this system. Although sometimes listed as an RS CVn system, this binary is now more accurately labeled as a naked T Tauri-type star. See Makarov2007 for more info.

notes4.Name: ----HD 220140 A
notes4.Note: Gaia DR3 lists this as a possible RS CVn variable with a best_class_score of 0.7.

notes4.Name: ZZ Psc
notes4.Note: Gaia DR3 lists this as a WD variable.

notes4.Name: G 190-28 & G 190-27
notes4.Note: BWL 59C is not associated with this system (WDS)

notes4.Name: --G 190-27
notes4.Note: Is itself a double (Bowler2015a). Bowler2015a measure a median delta magnitude of 0.35 mag, which we use to decompose the composite type into individual types of M4.5 and M5, which we in turn use to estimate individual masses.

notes4.Name: G 273-59 AB
notes4.Note: SB (Fouque2018). See more detailed info in CardonaGuillen2021, who argue that this binary is part of a dispersed group with BD-17 6768 AB and HD 221503. CardonaGuillen2021 estimate types of the individual components of M2-M2.5 and M3-M3.5, which we use for our estimated masses.

notes4.Name: BD+19 5116 AB
notes4.Note: Cvetkovic2010 derive a total dynamical mass of 0.590 M_Sun (with no uncertainty listed). LMP 24C is not associated with this system (Gaia DR2) and LMP 24D is assumed to be unassociated as well.

notes4.Name: --BD-17 6768 AB
notes4.Note: Has two entries in Gaia eDR3 and only one in Gaia DR2, but none of these has a parallax or proper motion solution. See more detailed info in CardonaGuillen2021, who argue that this binary is part of a dispersed group with G273-59 AB and HD 221503. CardonaGuillen2021 quotes nearly equal-mags in G_BP, G_RP, and G for the two components, so we assume that the individual types are identical to that of the composite. We use these to estimate the individual masses.

notes4.Name: --HD 221503
notes4.Note: LAF 73D is assumed to be unassociated. See more detailed info in CardonaGuillen2021, who argue that this star is part of a dispersed group with G273-59 AB and BD-17 6768 AB.

notes4.Name: CWISE J233817.04-732930.3
notes4.Note: Estimates are distance 19.9 pc and spectral type T8.5 (Kirkpatrick2024).

notes4.Name: CWISE J233819.49-385421.2
notes4.Note: Estimate is distance 18.5 pc (Kirkpatrick2024).

notes4.Name: gamma Cep AB
notes4.Note: SB (SBC9) split by Neuhauser2007.

notes4.Name: iota Psc
notes4.Note: BUP 240B and C are not associated with this star (WDS).

notes4.Name: BD+82 733 AB
notes4.Note: Gaia DR3 has NSS=2 -- non_linear_spectro (FirstDegreeTrendSB1). The G_BP-G_RP, J-Ks, and J-W2 colors suggest a composite type of K4, which we assume as the type of the primary, since this is an SB1. We use that type for the mass estimate of the primary. We adopt a wide range of possible lower masses for the secondary.

notes4.Name: --G 130-6
notes4.Note: Double (Jodar2013, Lamman2020). Lamman2020 measure a delta i' magnitude of 1.46 mag. Using this delta magnitude and the composite spectral type, we estimate individual spectral types of M3 and M4-M4.5. We use these types to estimate individual masses.

notes4.Name: CWISE J234426.81-475502.6
notes4.Note: Expected parallax is 59.8 mas (Kirkpatrick2021a).

notes4.Name: G 273-130 AB
notes4.Note: Double (Mason2018b, Montagnier2006). There are two sources within 1.1 arcsec in Gaia eDR3, but neither has a parallax or proper motion. There is no entry for this source at all in Gaia DR2. Montagnier2006 measure a delta J of 0.15 mag and a delta K' of 0.14 mag. Using the composite type and these delta mags, we estimate individual types of M4.5 and M4.5, which we use for our mass estimates.

notes4.Name: CWISE J235120.60-700026.2
notes4.Note: Estimates are distance 13.1 pc and spectral type Y0 (Kirkpatrick2024).

notes4.Name: HD 223778 AB
notes4.Note: BU 996C is not associated with this system (Gaia DR2). Component BU 996 B is the more widely separated component. Tokovinin2006 says A-B are separated by 4.6 arcsec and have a 258-yr period. The Cvetkovic2010 mass is for the entire triple system.

notes4.Name: --HD 223778 A
notes4.Note: SBC9 gives both components as having K3 V types. Ducati2011 call this an SB2. Gaia DR3 has NSS=1 -- acceleration_astro (Acceleration7). We use these type estimates for our mass estimates.

notes4.Name: --HD 223778 B
notes4.Note: This component has no parallax or proper motion in Gaia eDR3.

notes4.Name: BD+28 4660
notes4.Note: CRI 30B is not associated with this star (Gaia DR2).

notes4.Name: RX J2354.8+3831
notes4.Note: BWL 62B is not associated (WDS).

notes4.Name: BD-06 6318 AB
notes4.Note: SB (Baroch2021). See Vrijmoet2022, who measure a delta I of 4.3 mag. Using the composite type, we estimate individual types of M2.5 and M6.5. We use these to estimate individual masses.

notes4.Name: CWISEP J235644.78-481456.3
notes4.Note: Expected parallax is 57.6 mas (Kirkpatrick2021a) and estimated spectral type is Y0.5 (Meisner2020a).

notes4.Name: LP 704-15 & LP 704-14
notes4.Note: See Bowler2015b for specifics on this quadruple system.

notes4.Name: --LP 704-15
notes4.Note: Is itself a visual binary, 0.5 arcsec separation, of components Aa and Ab. Bowler2015b measure a delta H magnitude of 3.1 mag. Using this delta magnitude and the fact that the Aa component is an equal-magnitude binary, we can decompose this triple system into components of M3, M3, and M5.5, which we use for the individual mass estimates.

notes4.Name: ----LP 704-15 Aa
notes4.Note: Is itself an SB2 with components Aa1 and Aa2.

notes4.Name: --LP 704-14
notes4.Note: A physical binary of separation 20 arcsec with LP 704-15.

notes4.Name: G 129-47
notes4.Note: CRC 42B is not associated according to the WDS, but neither Gaia DR2 or eDR3 report a parallax or proper motion for this source. However, a finder chart comprised of DSS1 and DSS2 digitized scans along with digital frames from 2MASS, WISE, UHS, and PanSTARRS clearly show this source not to be co-moving with G 129-47.

notes4.Name: Wolf 1051 AB
notes4.Note: SB3 (Baroch2021). See also Vrijmoet2022, who measure a median delta I of 2.4 mag between the A and B components. Baroch2021 measure mass ratios of M_B/M_A= 0.549 and M_Bb/M_Ba = 0.937. Along with these mass ratios, we assume that the composite type is the same as that of the A component, and derive our mass estimates accordingly.

notes4.Name: BD+45 4378 AB
notes4.Note: SB2 (Fouque2018). See also Goldin2007 for an orbital solution. Source has no parallax or proper motion in Gaia eDR3. Because this is an SB2, we tentatively assume two components of the same type as the composite and estimate their masses accordingly.

notes4.Name: L 433-153 AB
notes4.Note: Source has no parallax or proper motion in Gaia eDR3. WDS says an orbit solution exists for this binary. Listed as a double in Vrijmoet2020. Gaia DR3 lists this as a possible LPV! The WDS lists a delta magnitude of 0.5 mag (presumably at V band), which we use to decompose the composte type into individual type estimates of M4 and M4-M4.5. We use these types for our mass estimates.
